subject: riotInterceptor
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: corporate riot-control interceptor with a water cannon and neon light bars.
Style: Cyberpunk 2077.
reasoning:
I'm designing an armored riot-control interceptor vehicle with a water cannon turret, neon light bars, and corporate decals in a cyberpunk palette, built as a static model using box-based geometry without joints since it's a vehicle rather than a creature.

I'm planning the dimensions and layout: roughly 5.2m long, 2.3m wide, 2.4m tall, with wheels resting on the ground, and sketching helper functions for boxes, glow effects, and SVG textures like hazard stripes, logos, and visor lights. I'm deciding to build the hull mainly from boxes rather than lofts for simplicity and safety.

Plotting hull outline points...

For paint, I'll use a panelled dark gunmetal texture from the clockwork kit to give the body a riveted, segmented look, then work on dark cylindrical wheel arches with box covers over the wheels.

Now I'm planning the wheel layout — three axles along the hull with cylindrical wheels outside the body width, hubs with a small neon glow ring, and plain dark tread color with a hubcap texture.

Adding fender boxes over each wheel and a thin cyan underglow strip along the lower armor skirt...

For the front, I'm adding a ram bar bumper with a hazard-striped texture and bull bar uprights, plus slim glowing headlight strips in cyan and magenta near the top of the front slope for that cyberpunk look.

Now I'm working out the windshield geometry -- calculating the slope vector and normal direction so I can place an angled plane between the hood and roof line, sizing it to match the diagonal distance.

I also need to plan the side windows: slim armored slits positioned along the sloped roofline, estimating the roof height at different z-positions to fit the windows flush against the body surface.

I want to add a corporate decal on the side panel, something like "NOVACORP" with "CIVIL ORDER DIVISION" or "RIOT CONTROL" lettering, and I need to work out the mirroring so the text reads correctly when viewed from outside on both the left and right side planes.

Now I'm placing the roof lighting: a glowing light bar across the cab roof near the front, plus a rack box with blue/red coloring, positioned above the cab roof height.

I'm also adding a rear roof neon strip along the edges and a water cannon turret mounted on the rear roof with a cylindrical base, boxy turret body, and a forward-angled barrel positioned over the cab.

Adding glowing level gauge, hoses curving to the turret, and the tapered barrel rod with nozzle rings angled slightly upward over the cab roof, then starting the turret base shape...

Still writing turret geometry...

I'm shaping the LRAD horn rods with flat glowing ends, then thinking about skipping tear gas launcher pods in favor of a custom dirty/mud paint function for the lower hull with panel lines and wear highlights.

Now I'm adding a neon accent stripe along the beltline with glowing magenta boxes.

Still placing hull details...

I'll settle the hood plate tilt slightly for the slope angle, then move to the front license plate—placing a yellow "OPS-0451" plate on the bumper's front face, aligning it with the bumper box dimensions and the hazard-striped texture covering the box.

Now I'm adding a push bar with angled rods and a headlight grille guard made of thin vertical bars near the front, then shifting to the rear with a dark bumper and glowing red vertical tail light strips.

For the wheels, I'm building layered cylinders for tire, hub, and a glowing torus ring accent, plus a spoked disc texture for the hub detail.

Checking the wheel cylinder geometry with 12 segments so the sink into the floor stays within tolerance, then placing the undercarriage box for ground clearance. For personality, I'm thinking about giving the vehicle a face-like front with angled headlights as glowing eyes.

Designing slanted headlight shapes as extruded outlines...

Placing the glowing eye positioning with thickness and slope geometry, and reconsidering the grille so it doesn't collide with the eye shapes by shifting the eyes outward.

I'm sketching the texture list—hazard stripes, side text, windshield, emblem, hubcap, plate, turret eye, gauges, grille, rear panel—then planning a windshield texture with cyan glass gradient and HUD scanlines, plus cage bars across the windshield for an armored look.

Now adding side mirrors with camera boxes and support arms, rear antenna rods with glowing magenta tips, and a textured water tank cylinder along the rear.

Actually simpler to put the gauge circle on the tank's rear end cap, facing outward at the back, sized to fit within the radius. For the hoses, I'm planning a connecting sweep from the tank's side to the turret base rather than tank-front to turret-rear since those points sit too close together.

Now mapping out the barrel details: adding reinforcing rings along the barrel length using lerp positions between two endpoints, then a nozzle rod at the tip.

Positioning the turret body box above the base lathe, checking it contains barrel A properly within its front face, then shaping the body with a chamfered wedge profile extruded for a more angular armored look.

Placing the sensor pod box and lens with the eye texture facing forward. Then I'm adding thin glowing cyan strips along the barrel sides for a pressure-line effect, and starting the cab roof lightbar housing positioned on the flat part of the roof.

Now I'm positioning the lightbar's lens segments alternating magenta and cyan on top, then adding glowing neon edge strips running along the roof borders near the turret base.

I'm deciding against Japanese text decals since fonts won't render reliably, opting for a plain skirt panel between the wheel wells with a magenta underglow box tucked beneath the hull bottom for visibility.

Skipping the hazard chevron decal, ladder, and crowd sirens for simplicity, I'm focusing on rear details like taillights, door frame, and a spike strip dispenser box. I'm setting the paint palette to navy, steel, magenta, cyan, yellow, and dark accents, then building the hull's panelled texture with small rivets and defining the seam ink color.

Now I'm setting up a 2048px paint canvas and helper functions for boxes and glowing lamp parts, then sketching a hazard stripe SVG pattern with diagonal yellow chevrons on a dark background for the fenders and hull trim.

I'm also designing the side decal texture with layered text—"NOVACORP" in bold white with a cyan outline, smaller enforcement labels in magenta, plus chevron accents—on a transparent background so it reads as a decal over the hull, and planning the windshield texture with a dark teal gradient and angled semi-transparent reflection streaks.

Still writing SVG textures... I'm now sketching the emblem as a hexagonal corp logo with cyan stroke and a magenta "N" shape, a hubcap with radial spokes, a yellow license plate reading "OPS-0451", a glowing red-iris eye texture, a slitted grille panel, and a labeled pressure gauge, while considering how to add door seam details to the cab.

Finishing up the overall structure, I'll return the builder root and make sure imports like paint, mix, noise, and lerp are in place before extruding the hull shape with the right thickness and bevel settings.

I'm sizing the fender covers relative to the wheel wells so they sit just above the tire radius, positioning them along the axle line, and checking the hood profile clears the front wheel. Then I'm adding the cage rods with a steel sweep color using the rod helper, and starting on the mirror geometry next.

Now I'm placing the rear lighting and bumper elements: glowing red taillights sized against the hull's rear face, a hazard panel, a rear bumper box, and a license plate positioned on the bumper's back face. I'm double-checking that the lerp helper returns a proper vector before passing it in, then moving to sketch barrel rings along the gun length.

Writing cylinder/rod code...
